## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Adhikaraṇasamatha* section of the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* (Bu-Vb As1–7), translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali as *The settling of legal issues*, comprises the canonical exposition and analysis of the seven procedural rules for settling disputes and legal questions (*adhikaraṇa*) arising within the Buddhist monastic order [SuttaCentral].
Text-reuse data computed by DharmaNexus demonstrates extensive internal and cross-canonical connections [DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali tradition, the text shares extensive passages with the rule lists of both the *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* (Pm Bu) and the *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* (Pm Bi), as well as its direct female counterpart in the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* (Bi-Vb As1–7) [DharmaNexus]. It also exhibits significant textual overlap with other canonical Vinaya treatments of dispute resolution, notably the *Samathakkhandhaka* (Kd 14) and the *Parivāra*'s *Samathabheda* (Pvr 5), and with the doctrinal expositions of the seven settlement methods found in Sutta texts such as the *Sāmagāma Sutta* (MN 104) and the *Sattakanipāta* of the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 7) [DharmaNexus]. Commentarial and sub-commentarial transmission is reflected in matches with the *Bhikkhupātimokkhapāḷi* (Tika Vin04t) and the *Kaṅkhāvitaraṇīpurāṇa-ṭīkā* (Tika Vin09t) [DharmaNexus]. Cross-linguistically, DharmaNexus aligns the text with Sanskrit recensions of the *Prātimokṣasūtra* and *Bhikṣuṇīvinaya*, the Tibetan *Prātimokṣasūtra* (D0002), and Tibetan Vinaya commentaries including the *Pratimokṣasūtravṛtti* (D4107) and *Pratimokṣasūtraṭīkāvinayasamuccaya* (D4106-3) [DharmaNexus].
None of the secondary literature matches retrieved in the research dossier directly examine this text, consisting entirely of false-positive matches for the string 'as 1' or citations of the Mahāyāna treatise *Abhidharmasamuccaya*.
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
